main_text.l: cernat ab æterno, est absurdum, quod ta-
men admittunt Remonstrantes, quando docent
Deum ab æterno homines eligere quoniam
credunt: at vero non absurdum, sed orthodo-
xum est, nos credendo efficere ut Deus nos in
Christo justos declaret conscientiis nostris &
pronunciet, adeoque nos credendo efficere
ut cessent effectus iræ & displicentiæ Dei mo-
do, pactioni euangelicæ, convenientissimo,
quo sensu nos fidem justificationis instrumen-
tum esse credimus, non quod fides qua opus
sit nostræ justitiæ pars, sed quod fide ample-
ctamur Christum datum à Deo nobis in justi-
tiam fidem manu quasi apprehendere justitiam
Christi aut remissionem attrahere nugas meras
vocant, notitiam, assensum aut applicatione esse
actionem instrumentalem vocant. Sed quia fide

l.i: remissionem peccatorum, ex promisso Dei, quam si fides
veluti instrumentum à Deo data esset ad obtinendam

main_text.l: dicitur. Sed R.1.[?] Fidem instrumentum respectu
Dei actu justificantis nemo nostrum dixit: at re-
spectu justificationis passive in nostram con-
scientiam terminatæ instrumentum, hoc sen-
su appellamus, non quod fides ulla organica
causalitate Christi justitiam producat; nugan-
tur qui hoc nobis imputent, aut quod actu
reali justitiam Christi attrahat, sicut manus
pauperis eleemosynam attrahat (omnis enim
similitudo claudicat) sed quod impleta per

pleto

page.notes: The marginal note "Apol f. 112" is printed in the right margin beside the line "fide præstita"; its placement in the transcription follows that line. "con-scientiam" is split at the line end; an underline stroke runs under the word "scientiam" in the scan, which may be a printer's or reader's mark and is not transcribed. "R.1." has a special form of R before the 1 that I could not read with certainty. The mark after "peccatorum" appears as a printed question mark and is kept as printed. The text is printed in roman with italic passages; "Remonstrantes" and the passage from "quia fide" to "dicitur." are italic.
